transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... I guess I'm here because I haven't really been sleeping. It's been going on since this... warehouse inspection I had to do for work. I just kind of lie in bed replaying bits of it. And if I do manage to drift off, I just... I wake up sweating, wide awake. Almost like I'm right back near that blast.
Can you describe what goes through your mind when you wake up sweating? Do you feel like you're reliving the blast or seeing parts of it again?

Yeah... I guess I see parts of it. It's... well, it actually happens during the day, too. I'll just be at work, reviewing a policy or... looking at a loss report, and... I don't know, I just suddenly get hit with this really sharp image. Of the worker on the floor. And the soot in the air. My body just sort of... reacts to it before I can even stop it. So... yeah. That's mostly what it is.
Since the incident, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened at the warehouse?

Um... yeah, I guess. I haven't really been looking at the file for that warehouse. I just kind of... push it to the side. And if a call comes in about an industrial account, I just let it go to voicemail. I can't really... even just opening the emails about it makes my stomach drop, so I just... don't.
Since the incident, have you noticed any changes in your mood or the way you think about yourself or the world?

Um... I don't know. I haven't really thought about it like that. I just... I guess I feel a bit off, but... I don't really know how to describe it. I haven't noticed any big changes in how I think about the world or anything. Just... tired, mostly.
Since the incident, have you noticed yourself feeling more irritable, angry, or easily startled? Or maybe having trouble concentrating on tasks that you used to handle easily?

Um... yeah, I guess. I mean, I have been a little more irritable. I actually... I snapped at one of the junior analysts the other day. He just asked a simple question about a spreadsheet, and I... I just laid into him. It was way harsher than I meant to be. I felt pretty embarrassed after, honestly. I don't usually talk to people like that. So... yeah, I guess I've been a bit on edge.
Since the incident, have you found yourself feeling ongoing fear, guilt, or anger, especially when thinking about what happened during the warehouse inspection?

Um... I don't really know. I try not to think about the inspection at all, to be honest. I wouldn't say I feel... angry or guilty or anything like that. Just... I don't know. I just don't really want to think about it.
How long have these symptoms been going on since the warehouse inspection?
Um... about a week. It started right after that inspection... you know, when the explosion happened. So, yeah... just a week.
Have these symptoms continued beyond the first month since the warehouse explosion?
Um... no. Like I just said, it's only been about a week since it happened. So... no. Not a month.
Since the incident, have you had ongoing feelings of fear, anger, or guilt, even when you're not actively thinking about the warehouse explosion?
Um... I think I just answered that. Like I said, I don't really feel... angry or guilty or whatever. I just try to keep my mind off it, mostly.
Have these symptoms been affecting your ability to do your job, interact with others, or carry out your usual daily activities?

Um... yeah, I guess. At work, mostly. I've... missed some deadlines on a few underwriting reviews. And, um... I've started handing off some of the industrial account calls I'm supposed to be managing. I just... I don't know, I just took on this role recently, so... it's probably making me look pretty unreliable. But... yeah.
Since the incident, have you noticed any negative changes in your thoughts or mood, such as feeling hopeless, detached, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
Um... no, not really. I'm not... hopeless or anything. I just... I don't know, I just try to go about my day like normal. I haven't really noticed feeling like that.
Since the incident, have you had trouble relaxing, felt constantly on guard, or been more jumpy or easily startled than usual?

Um... yeah, I guess I've been a little jumpy. Like, at work... if a printer jams, or a door slams, or... someone just walks up behind my desk... I just, I jump. Like something really bad is happening. And then... it just takes me a few minutes to, um, calm down again. So... yeah.
Have your symptoms continued for more than one month since the warehouse explosion?
Um... no, not that long. It's... it's only been about a week. Ever since the, um... the inspection at the warehouse. When it happened.
Have your symptoms continued for more than one month since the warehouse explosion?
Um... like I just said, no. It hasn't been a month. Just... about a week.
Have your symptoms been ongoing for at least one month now?
I... I feel like we just went over this. No. It hasn't been a month. It's just been a week... since the inspection.
Have your symptoms been ongoing for at least one month now?
I... I really don't understand why you keep asking me that. No. Like I just said, it's only been about a week... since the warehouse inspection. When the explosion happened. Not a month.
